sources.title: Batch 0058 frozen repository source context for AQS/ReentrantLock fairness
Frozen OpenJDK 21 GA primary-source research for ReentrantLock and AQS

claims.text: All frozen repository variants ask how AQS/ReentrantLock realizes fair versus non-fair lock acquisition; the candidate stays on that mechanism and does not invent project history.

OpenJDK 21 GA AQS supplies synchronization-state and FIFO wait-queue/acquire/release mechanics while allowing barging policies; ReentrantLock subclasses supply the actual fair/non-fair admission policy.

The non-fair synchronizer can CAS an available state without predecessor checks, while the fair synchronizer gates the CAS on queue-state/predecessor checks; both use the AQS queue after acquisition failure.
Both policies preserve owner reentrancy by incrementing the hold count, and release only clears ownership when the hold count reaches zero.

The candidate explicitly preserves OpenJDK's fairness boundaries: fairness is a lock-admission policy rather than JVM/OS scheduling fairness, and untimed tryLock() does not honor the fairness setting.
